thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: streaming-pipeline: p99 tail latency > 5s (SLO breach) across us-west-2. Auto-pager triggered (severity: high).

pager-maya: taking page. seeing alerts for streaming responses, lots of stalls/zero-length chunks. anyone oncall for runtime?

sre-kyle: I'm oncall. pulling graphs now — p95 ~ 800ms, p99 ~ 6.2s for /v1/stream, error rate spiking to 1.8% on proxy 504/timeout.

liam-runtime: got it. initial hypothesis: proxy write buffers filling because some clients stopped reading (slow consumers). downstream write errors show EPIPE on the proxy-to-client side.

anya-cs: We already got a flag from a customer (acme-inc) complaining about partially delivered responses. They're on a high-volume integration.

sre-kyle: quick triage notes:
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streams/streaming-tail?orgId=1&from=now-15m to=now (watch p99)
- Proxy nodes: proxy-usw2-batch{5..8} show elevated write queues and retransmits.
- Ingress LB shows steady RPS; origin serving runtime appears healthy (token CPU fine), latched on KV cache hits unchanged.

liam-runtime: attaching a short log snippet from proxy:
```
2026-03-15T14:08:12Z proxy-usw2-batch6 WARN write_fail client_id=svc-123 err=EPIPE retry=0
2026-03-15T14:08:13Z proxy-usw2-batch7 WARN chunk_flush delay_ms=1200 queue_len=312
2026-03-15T14:08:14Z proxy-usw2-batch8 ERROR stalled_chunk client_id=svc-456 stall_ms=5200
```

sre-kyle: looks like slow consumer problem leading to backpressure in proxy. That cascades to longer flush times and higher tail latency. If clients stop reading, proxy buffers fill and stall other streams.

pager-maya: mitigation plan?

liam-runtime: immediate mitigations we can do now:
1) Enable aggressive keepalive/timeout for idle client sockets for a short window to drop stuck connections: `kubectl exec -it proxy -- curl -X POST /admin/conn-timeout -d '{"idle_ms":30000}'`
2) Reduce `max_inflight_batches` on proxy to reduce head-of-line blocking: `config set proxy.max_inflight_batches 16`
3) Enable chunking fallback to non-streaming (graceful degrade) for customer-tier=standard so we avoid SSE stalls for those clients.

sre-kyle: I'm going to roll the timeout change on a single proxy pool (proxy-usw2-batch6) and observe. will annotate changes.

ops-bot: change-request: POST /admin/conn-timeout applied to proxy-usw2-batch6 by kyle (runbook-step-3).

sre-kyle: applied to batch6. watching. p99 dropped from 6.2s -> 4.1s within 90s. queue_len decreased ~60%.

liam-runtime: good sign. I'm going to push config to batch7 as well and simultaneously reduce max_inflight_batches at 2pmPT.

anya-cs: FYI paging timeline and affected customers so CS can notify: acme-inc (high traffic), shoply, and two smaller integrations. acme reports partial payloads. mark as incident and draft message?

pager-maya: @anya-cs please prepare templated message: brief impact, workarounds (switch to polling endpoint), ETA for mitigation.

liam-runtime: pushed max_inflight change to batch7. also toggled fallback for standard-tier to buffered-response mode.

sre-kyle: after batch7 change p99 ~ 2.3s, error-rate fell to 0.4%. still seeing some stale connections on batch8, will cycle nodes in that pool.

ops-bot: rolling restart initiated for proxy-usw2-batch8 (strategy: one-by-one, drain with 60s grace).

sre-kyle: restart finished for batch8. metrics: p99 now 1.1s, p95 ~ 420ms. chunking stalls reduced drastically.

liam-runtime: root cause hypothesis: a subset of client integrations opened long-lived SSE connections but had intermittent network issues causing them to stop reading; proxy buffering policy allowed large per-connection buffers so stalled clients consumed memory and headroom, producing backpressure. We need to tighten defaults and add aggressive detection of stalled chunk flush.

anya-cs: customers notified: acme-inc acknowledged, toggled to buffered endpoint and their errors dropped. shoply applied workaround and is stable.

sre-kyle: immediate action items (assigned):
- liam-runtime: follow up PR to add `stalled_chunk_detector` to proxy with metrics and kill-switch by EOD.
- liam-runtime: reduce default per-connection buffer cap and lower keepalive to 30s for streaming for next deploy.
- kyle: draft incident ticket and severity writeup; collect traces and pcap for batch6-8 windows.
- anya-cs: customer comms + escalation logs for acme/shoply.

liam-runtime: starting a small patch now. code snippet for detector logic:```
if (chunk_flush_ms > 2000 && retries > 3) {
  emit_metric("proxy.stalled_chunk_detected")
  close_connection(client_id)
}
```

sre-kyle: for next oncall handoff: @sarah-oncall you'll take over at 18:00 PT. current status: mitigated (p99 back to 1.1s), error-rate nominal but open action items and PR in review. please verify rollout of buffer cap change tomorrow morning.

sarah-oncall: ack. I'll watch the canary and ensure there's no regression. will also follow up on the postmortem and link to the incident channel.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-1102 (link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-1102). severity: high -> tracking SLO regression and customer impact.

anya-cs: logged customer comms drafts in INC-2026-1102 and assigned to me for final send after engineering confirm.

sre-kyle: note for postmortem: add timeline with metrics, list of mitigations and their measured effect (conn-timeout -> p99 down 34%, max_inflight -> additional 48% reduction, restart batch8 -> final stabilization). Also include suggestions: default buffer cap decrease, stalled_chunk detector, and a canary for large-file streaming.

pager-maya: thx everyone. will mark this thread resolved once sarah confirms canary stable and PR merged.

sarah-oncall: confirmed 2 hours later: canary stable, no recurring alerts. handing off to day team. closing watch.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-1102 updated: status -> monitoring.

sre-kyle: final note: add regression alert to runbook to auto-fallback affected clients to buffered endpoint when p99 > 2s for 5m.

anya-cs: will send post-incident customer note template to affected accounts by EOD.

pager-maya: resolved in ops dashboard, closing this thread. :white_check_mark:
